sections.heading: Asking you to order my path
sections.text: Lord, your power has no limit, and your wisdom never fails. Please arrange the details of my life so that they do not block me, discourage me, or get in the way of what you are doing. Keep me from being dragged into useless conflict. Protect me from harm, and protect me even more from sin that would twist the gifts, energy, and growth you have given me.
theological_themes: The believer depends on God to remove hindrances and preserve integrity
Spiritual gifts and zeal need protection from corruption by sin

scripture_references.connection: This passage calls God’s people to trust his wisdom rather than their own understanding, with the promise that he will make their paths straight. It supports the prayer’s request for God to order the road ahead rather than leaving the believer to self-directed plans.

Peter teaches that gifts are entrusted by God and must be used in dependence on him so that he receives glory. That grounds the concern that even good gifts, zeal, and service must be guarded from sinful misuse.

sections.heading: Keeping me from work you have not given me
sections.text: Help me do the duty you have actually placed in front of me, not chase some foolish plan of my own. Do not let me pour myself into work you will not bless. I want to serve you cleanly, without bringing shame on your name or creating burdens I had no right to take on.
theological_themes: Obedience is better than self-made ambition
God’s blessing matters more than visible activity
Service should be done with integrity and humility

scripture_references.connection: Paul says believers are created in Christ for good works that God prepared beforehand. This supports asking to recognize and walk in God-given work rather than inventing self-serving labor.
The psalm teaches that labor apart from the Lord’s building and guarding is ultimately vain. It fits the prayer’s concern not to spend life on work God has not called or blessed.

sections.heading: Hiding under your protection
sections.text: Let me live close to you, under your shelter. Be my refuge when danger is obvious and when it is hidden; when people speak cruelly, when malice is aimed at me, when careless words wound, and when relationships pull me toward sin. Keep me through the risks of youth, the pressures of middle age, the griefs of old age, and the fear of death. Father, hold me where I cannot hold myself.
theological_themes: God is the believer’s refuge in visible and invisible dangers
Human life is vulnerable at every stage
The fear of death is brought to God rather than denied

scripture_references.connection: The original prayer clearly draws on this psalm’s language of dwelling in God’s shelter amid danger by day and night. The passage supports praying for refuge in God while trusting his protective care.
David speaks of God sheltering his people from human plots and the strife of tongues. This directly illuminates the prayer’s request for protection from malice, slander, and destructive speech.
Hebrews says Christ’s death frees those held in lifelong slavery by the fear of death. That gives gospel depth to the prayer’s plea for courage when facing mortality.

sections.heading: Depending on your Spirit to keep me moving forward
sections.text: I depend on you completely for strength, wisdom, and comfort. Uphold me by your Spirit. But do not let me be satisfied with merely not falling apart or not falling into obvious sin. Keep me moving forward. Make me steady, fruitful, and generous in the work you give me to do. Strengthen me deep inside for every part of following Christ.
theological_themes: The Holy Spirit sustains, counsels, and strengthens believers
Christian perseverance includes growth, not mere survival
God equips his people for faithful work

scripture_references.connection: Paul prays that believers would be strengthened with power through the Spirit in the inner person. This closely supports the request for inward strength for the whole Christian life.

Because of Christ’s resurrection, Paul urges believers to be steadfast and always abounding in the Lord’s work. This grounds the prayer’s desire not only to be preserved but to keep advancing in faithful service.

sections.heading: Handing everything back to you
sections.text: Everything I treasure, I place in your keeping: my identity in Christ, my body and soul, my abilities, my character, my reputation, my usefulness, my marriage, my children, my friends, my work, today, tomorrow, and the hour when my life ends. Take all of it. It already belongs to you. I belong to you too—now and forever.
theological_themes: The believer’s identity is renewed in Christ
All possessions, relationships, gifts, and the future belong to God
Surrender rests in belonging to the Lord in life and death

scripture_references.connection: Paul teaches that whether believers live or die, they belong to the Lord. This supports the prayer’s final entrusting of present life, future, and death to God.
Paul reminds Christians that they are not their own because they were bought with a price. That grounds the prayer’s surrender of body, soul, gifts, and whole life to God.
This passage locates the believer’s life and future hope in Christ. It supports the prayer’s language of a renewed name and identity in Christ, held safely by God.

content_provenance.original_author: Unattributed Puritan source (compiled and edited by Arthur Bennett)
content_provenance.original_source: The Valley of Vision: A Collection of Puritan Prayers and Devotions, ed. Arthur Bennett (The Banner of Truth Trust)
content_provenance.source_copyright_status: Compilation, titles and arrangement in copyright (Banner of Truth, 1975); underlying Puritan sources are public domain.
content_provenance.modern_version_note: Contemporary prayer based on the theological themes and ideas of the historical source; not a reproduction of the original wording.

theological_issues_identified: The original’s Psalm 91 language could be misread as a guarantee that no physical harm, illness, slander, grief, or death will touch the believer. This adaptation keeps the strong plea for protection while framing it as trust in God’s refuge and preserving care, not as a promise of immunity from suffering.

The line about not laboring at work God will not bless could be misunderstood as saying faithful work will always avoid debt, disgrace, or failure. The adaptation renders it as a request for integrity, calling, and freedom from self-made burdens rather than a prosperity claim.

The original assumes a male speaker with a wife and children. The adaptation uses “my marriage” rather than “my wife” to preserve the household entrustment without unnecessarily restricting the prayer to men.
significant_interpretive_choices: “Stand between me and all strife” was rendered as protection from being dragged into useless conflict, because the surrounding lines focus on dangers that can harm both the person and their service to God.
“No sin corrupt my gifts, zeal, attainments” was interpreted as a prayer that good spiritual gifts and progress not be twisted by pride, ambition, or moral failure.

“All my jewels” was taken to mean everything the speaker treasures most—identity, relationships, reputation, gifts, work, future, and death—and was kept concrete rather than reduced to a general statement of surrender.
